keyWhy.ko: 핵심은 «시장 경제에서 가격은 공급과 수요의 균형으로 정해진다(원리)» 와 «그래도 공급과 수요의 관계가 가격이 변하는 이유를 설명해 준다(결론)» 입니다. 초록색 문장이 정답이에요.
keyWhy.en: The key ideas are the principle (prices are largely set by the balance between supply and demand) and the conclusion (this relationship still helps explain why prices change). The green sentences are the answers.

qs.q: Why do prices usually fall when supply increases but demand does not change?
qs.qko: 수요는 그대로인데 공급이 늘면 왜 보통 가격이 내려가나요?
opts: Because sellers must compete for customers
Because buyers compete for limited goods
Because the government always sets lower prices
evs: When supply increases while demand does not change, sellers must compete for customers, so prices usually fall.
When demand rises but supply stays the same, buyers compete for limited goods, and prices tend to go up.
Of course, real markets are also affected by other factors, such as government rules, advertising, and unexpected events.
A high price tells producers that people want more of a product, encouraging them to make more.
why: 본문에 공급이 늘면 «sellers must compete for customers» 라고 나와요. 파는 사람끼리 손님을 두고 경쟁하니 가격이 내려가요. 두 번째 보기는 수요가 늘 때의 이야기예요.
The text says sellers must compete for customers, so prices fall. The second option describes what happens when demand rises.

qs.q: In 'When the next harvest is plentiful,' what does 'plentiful' mean?
qs.qko: 'When the next harvest is plentiful' 에서 'plentiful' 은 무슨 뜻인가요?
evs: When the next harvest is plentiful, the price falls again.
Because fewer cabbages reach the market, their price rises, sometimes sharply.
Supply is the amount of a product that sellers are willing to offer, while demand is the amount that buyers want to purchase.
A low price suggests that resources might be better used elsewhere.
why: 흉작 때는 배추가 적어서 가격이 올랐어요. plentiful 한 수확에는 가격이 다시 내려가니, 반대로 «양이 많다» 는 뜻이에요.
After a poor harvest there are fewer cabbages and the price rises. With a plentiful harvest the price falls, so plentiful means more than enough.

qs.q: How does a high price help the market get more of a product?
qs.qko: 높은 가격은 어떻게 시장에 그 상품이 더 많아지도록 도울까요?
opts: It signals that people want more, so producers make more
It tells buyers to stop shopping
It makes cabbages grow faster on farms
evs: A high price tells producers that people want more of a product, encouraging them to make more.
A low price suggests that resources might be better used elsewhere.
In a market economy, prices are largely set by the balance between supply and demand.
why: 가격은 중요한 신호를 보내고, 높은 가격은 생산자에게 사람들이 더 원한다고 알려 더 만들게 해요. 두 단서를 합치면 답이 나와요.
Prices send signals, and a high price tells producers people want more, encouraging them to make more.

ends: Why do concert tickets sometimes become so expensive?
콘서트 표는 왜 가끔 그렇게 비싸질까?
How do governments sometimes control prices?
